Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list of asks. Short answer: yes, we support both patterns, but the default for hosted customers is alerting + soft throttles rather than a hard block. Below is a concise summary you can attach to the PO; I’ll also include the formal PDF rate card and a suggested amendment if you want a hard cap.

Options we provide (hosted API):
1) Hard spend cap (enforceable):
   - Available as a contract amendment. When reached, API requests receive a 402/429 response (configurable) and sandboxed requests are blocked until the next billing period or a manual lift. Requires legal/ops sign-off and an up-front amendment (see attached amendment_overage_buffer.pdf).
2) Soft cap + alerts (default):
   - Real-time alerts (email + webhook) at configurable thresholds (80/90/100%).
   - Automatic throttling policy: reduce max tokens/requests-per-second when near cap to slow spend while preserving critical traffic.
3) Controlled overage buffer:
   - One-time buffer (e.g., 10–15% over committed) by sales approval. Billed on next invoice at standard rates or pre-negotiated capped overage rate.
4) Fallback routing:
   - When cost-sensitive, we can optionally route excess requests to a lower-cost model variant to keep applications online with reduced quality.

Billing/approval practice for overages:
- If a customer requests a buffer ahead of time, Sales creates a written amendment (DocuSign) that specifies the buffer and rate. Otherwise, standard behavior is to bill any usage beyond committed amounts on the following invoice with line-item detail and usage snapshots. We also support hold-for-PO where we temporarily suspend API keys pending procurement sign-off if the customer prefers no overages.

I’ve attached the November rate card and a short amendment template you can attach to your PO. Rishi — quick ask: are we ok to offer BrightLane a one-time 10% buffer while procurement completes the PO?

Best,
